name: Place a hold on a member's share
description: Places a hold on a share for a given reason, via MERIDIAN's entry -> review -> post flow. Doubly gated: irreversible like Funds Transfer/Open New Share (our own confirmation requirement), and additionally restricted to supervisors by MERIDIAN itself -- a teller reaches a real permission_denied business outcome right at the review step, before any commit button even exists for them to see.

preconditions.note: Assumes an authenticated operator session. Which operator matters here more than for any other MERIDIAN capability: a teller session hits permission_denied at the review step; only a supervisor session (e.g. super1) can reach and complete the final Apply Hold step.

success_checkpoint.description: Corrected against a real confirmed post as super1 -- the provisional guess 'HOLD PLACED' was wrong (the real heading is 'ACCOUNT HOLD APPLIED'), which surfaced as a hard_failure on the first verification attempt: the step-level checkpoint below already matched correctly, so s9 completed, but the mismatched success_checkpoint made the engine re-classify and treat the second post-resume failure as terminal. Fixed by using the real observed text.

For a teller session, classify() catches the resulting is not authorized to perform this function page as a permission_denied business outcome right here -- MERIDIAN checks supervisor authorization at review time for this capability, not just at the final commit like Funds Transfer/Open New Share. Confirmed via two separate discovery runs: as teller1, gave up immediately after this click with the real 'is not authorized to perform this function' page; as super1, this click correctly landed on the real CONFIRM ACCOUNT HOLD review screen instead.

Hand-authored, not discovered as-is -- even as super1, discovery correctly could not click this button itself (blocked: irreversible action requires confirmation), same reason as every other irreversible commit step in this repo. The review page itself also labels this 'IRREVERSIBLE ACTION' in bold, independent of anything our own system says.
Same proven pattern as funds_transfer/open_share's real success pages -- verified against a real applied hold (heading 'ACCOUNT HOLD APPLIED', 'Confirmation:' | 'CN480386' as sibling <td> cells).
